The DCTERMS term is broader: dcterms:references also covers pointers that are not citations. Same direction: A Cites B becomes A dcterms:references B.
Corresponding relationship; see relation-cites for endpoints and conditions. A includes B in a citation.
Corresponding relationship with the same direction: A HasPart B becomes A dcterms:hasPart B.
Corresponding relationship; see relation-haspart for endpoints and conditions. Keep A as the containing work and B as its part.
Corresponding relationship; see relation-hastranslation for endpoints and conditions. Preserve A as original and B as translation.
Corresponding relationship with the same direction: A HasVersion B becomes A dcterms:hasVersion B.
The DCTERMS term is broader: dcterms:isReferencedBy also covers pointers that are not citations. Same direction: A IsCitedBy B becomes A dcterms:isReferencedBy B.
Corresponding relationship with the same direction: A IsDerivedFrom B becomes A dcterms:source B.
Corresponding relationship; see relation-isderivedfrom for endpoints and conditions. Use derivation evidence; this does not replace supplement or version relations.

Associated relationship; see relation-isidenticalto for endpoints and conditions. DataCite content identity alone is insufficient for entity identity; do not equate two distinct files, versions or records merely because content matches.
The DCTERMS term is broader: it does not say which version came first. Same direction: A IsNewVersionOf B becomes A dcterms:isVersionOf B.
Corresponding relationship with the same direction: A IsObsoletedBy B becomes A dcterms:isReplacedBy B.
Both describe substantially the same resource in another format. Same direction: A IsOriginalFormOf B becomes A dcterms:hasFormat B.
Corresponding relationship with the same direction: A IsPartOf B becomes A dcterms:isPartOf B.
Corresponding relationship; see relation-ispartof for endpoints and conditions. Keep A as the part and B as the containing work.
The DCTERMS term is broader: it does not say which version came first. Same direction: A IsPreviousVersionOf B becomes A dcterms:hasVersion B.
The DCTERMS term is broader: publication in a journal or series is one kind of being part of something. Same direction: A IsPublishedIn B becomes A dcterms:isPartOf B.

The Schema.org term is broader. Corresponding relationship; see relation-ispublishedin for endpoints and conditions. Preserve the stronger publication relation in the source; bibliographic-location creates issue/volume nodes when known.
Corresponding relationship with the same direction: A IsReferencedBy B becomes A dcterms:isReferencedBy B.
Corresponding relationship with the same direction: A IsRequiredBy B becomes A dcterms:isRequiredBy B.
Corresponding relationship; see relation-isreviewedby for endpoints and conditions. The reviewed item A points to review B; B itemReviewed A is also valid when A lacks a suitable review domain.
Corresponding relationship; see relation-istranslationof for endpoints and conditions. A translated title alone is insufficient evidence of a translated work.
Both describe substantially the same resource in another format. Same direction: A IsVariantFormOf B becomes A dcterms:isFormatOf B.
Corresponding relationship with the same direction: A IsVersionOf B becomes A dcterms:isVersionOf B.
Corresponding relationship with the same direction: A Obsoletes B becomes A dcterms:replaces B.
Corresponding relationship with the same direction: A References B becomes A dcterms:references B.

The Schema.org term is narrower. Corresponding relationship; see relation-references for endpoints and conditions. References can exceed bibliographic citation; retain the source relation if this condition is not met.
Corresponding relationship with the same direction: A Requires B becomes A dcterms:requires B.
Corresponding relationship; see relation-reviews for endpoints and conditions. Correct direction: the review A points to the item B. schema:reviews is deprecated and has the opposite direction.
The DataCite category corresponds closely to the DCMI Type category.
The Schema.org term is narrower. Use VideoObject for a video encoding; moving-image works without an identified file retain their source type. See resource-types.
The Schema.org term is narrower. Grant only when an actual funding award is described; honors or nonfinancial awards require separate modeling. See resource-types.
DCMI Type Text is broader than the DataCite Book category; a target export must retain the more specific source type when needed.
The concepts describe books; do not infer a particular edition or physical copy.
A book work can be represented as Book. See resource-types.
DCMI Type Text is broader than the DataCite BookChapter category; a target export must retain the more specific source type when needed.
Wikidata chapter includes divisions of works beyond books; the target concept is broader.
A chapter within a book can be represented as Chapter; retain its parent book. See resource-types.
The DataCite category corresponds closely to the DCMI Type category.
Both describe purposely grouped resources or objects.
A collection of creative works can use Collection; collections of other entity types require another target model. See resource-types.
SoftwareSourceCode describes the source-bearing aspect; outputs and narrative may need additional nodes. See resource-types; value-to-class association only.
DCMI Type Text is broader than the DataCite ConferencePaper category; a target export must retain the more specific source type when needed.
The Schema.org term is broader. ScholarlyArticle can describe the paper; retain the conference-paper distinction. See resource-types.
Wikidata conference paper describes a document published in conference proceedings; DataCite also includes submissions intended for conference acceptance.
DCMI Type Text is broader than the DataCite ConferenceProceeding category; a target export must retain the more specific source type when needed.
The Schema.org term is broader. Represent the proceedings work generically unless a publication volume or book is actually established. See resource-types.
Both describe a collection of papers issued for an academic conference.
DCMI Type Text is broader than the DataCite DataPaper category; a target export must retain the more specific source type when needed.
The Schema.org term is broader. ScholarlyArticle can describe the paper; retain that its purpose is to describe data. See resource-types.
Both describe a scholarly publication focused on describing data.
The DataCite category corresponds closely to the DCMI Type category.
Both describe structured data; DCAT additionally situates datasets in an agent-published or curated catalog context.
Both describe a collection of data; this is concept alignment, not a generated Wikidata statement.
A dataset can be represented as Dataset. See resource-types.
DCMI Type Text is broader than the DataCite Dissertation category; a target export must retain the more specific source type when needed.
Both describe academic thesis work; qualification-level details require source preservation.
A thesis or dissertation can be represented as Thesis. See resource-types.
The DataCite category corresponds closely to the DCMI Type category.
The identified event can be represented as Event. See resource-types.
The DataCite category corresponds closely to the DCMI Type category.
Both describe a visual representation; no file format or licensing inference is implied.
The Schema.org term is narrower. Use ImageObject for an image encoding; a physical artwork may need another type. See resource-types.
Use Product only when the described instrument is a product; do not classify every measuring facility or prototype as a commercial offering. See resource-types; value-to-class association only.
The Schema.org term is broader. Use CreativeWork where applicable; interaction alone does not establish SoftwareApplication. See resource-types.
The DataCite category corresponds closely to the DCMI Type category.
DCMI Type Text is broader than the DataCite Journal category; a target export must retain the more specific source type when needed.
The Schema.org term is broader. A scholarly journal is represented as Periodical; retain journal specialization. See resource-types.
Both describe an academic periodical; preserve the source scholarly-publication context.
DCMI Type Text is broader than the DataCite JournalArticle category; a target export must retain the more specific source type when needed.
The Wikidata article concept also includes newspaper and magazine articles, beyond a journal article.
The Schema.org term is broader. Use ScholarlyArticle for a scholarly journal article; DataCite does not by itself establish peer-review status. See resource-types.
The Wikidata model concept includes physical and conceptual representations; DataCite Model describes abstract representations. No 3D restriction is imposed.
The Schema.org term is narrower. Only a genuine 3D model receives 3DModel; mathematical and conceptual models retain their source classification. See resource-types.
DCMI Type Text is broader than the DataCite OutputManagementPlan category; a target export must retain the more specific source type when needed.
The Schema.org term is broader. Represent the plan document as CreativeWork; its future-planning purpose does not make it a report automatically. See resource-types.
A data management plan covers a subset of the broader DataCite plans for research outputs, which may also include software and other outputs.
For the registered review document, DCMI Type Text is the broader category; the evaluation activity itself must not be typed as Text.
Wikidata review includes evaluations beyond scientific or professional peer review.
The Schema.org term is broader. A review work can be Review; retain peer-review purpose. See resource-types.
The Schema.org term is broader. Keep Thing unless a more specific physical type is established; do not assume every specimen is a Product. See resource-types.
The DataCite category corresponds closely to the DCMI Type category.
Both describe tangible objects; retain specific sample or material descriptions.
The Schema.org term is broader. A research poster can be a CreativeWork; retain Poster as additionalType text. See resource-types.
Both describe research posters for academic events; correspondence checked against the Wikidata conference-poster item.
DCMI Type Text is broader than the DataCite Preprint category; a target export must retain the more specific source type when needed.
The Schema.org term is broader. A scholarly preprint can be ScholarlyArticle; retain preprint status and do not infer peer review. See resource-types.
Both describe a scholarly paper before formal peer-reviewed publication.
The Schema.org term is broader. Describe presentation content as CreativeWork; a presentation event is a distinct entity. See resource-types.
The DataCite value describes a set of slides; the matching item is a slide deck, not the delivery event or a single slide.
Both describe a planned endeavor to achieve a goal using allocated resources.
Use Project when its organized-enterprise meaning fits; retain the source type otherwise. See resource-types.
DCMI Type Text is broader than the DataCite Report category; a target export must retain the more specific source type when needed.
Both describe a report document; a record-level conversion still requires independent bibliographic modeling.
A report work can be represented as Report. See resource-types.
The DataCite category corresponds closely to the DCMI Type category.
A provided service can be represented as Service. See resource-types.
Both cover software programs; DataCite separates computational notebooks into another category, so equivalence is not asserted.
Both describe computer software; DataCite excludes computational notebooks and includes source code, so exact equivalence is not asserted.
The Schema.org term is narrower. Runnable-application branch of resource-types; Software also includes source code.
The Schema.org term is narrower. Choose SoftwareSourceCode for source code and SoftwareApplication for a runnable application; retain broader Software classification. See resource-types.
The DataCite category corresponds closely to the DCMI Type category.
Both concern recorded audio content; an audio-record conversion requires separate graph and media modeling.
The Schema.org term is narrower. Use AudioObject for an audio encoding; retain work/file distinctions. See resource-types.
The Schema.org term is broader. Represent the standard document as CreativeWork; it is not necessarily a vocabulary or DefinedTermSet. See resource-types.
Both denote an established reference against which things can be evaluated; no restriction to metadata schemes is implied.
DCMI Type Text is broader than the DataCite StudyRegistration category; a target export must retain the more specific source type when needed.
The Schema.org term is broader. Represent the time-stamped registration plan as CreativeWork; do not equate it with a MedicalStudy or the study itself. See resource-types.
DataCite Text excludes separately enumerated textual types; DCMI Type Text also includes those types.
Wikidata text is broader; DataCite Text excludes separately enumerated textual resource types.
The Schema.org term is broader. Use CreativeWork for textual content; Text also includes physical publications and does not imply DigitalDocument. See resource-types.
The Schema.org term is broader. Retain workflow classification; choose SoftwareSourceCode only for executable source and HowTo only for instructions. See resource-types.
Both denote an organized sequence of activities; execution metadata is outside this correspondence.
The alternative-title kind corresponds to dcterms:alternative, the property that holds the title text.
The alternative-title kind corresponds to the property that holds the title text; see title-values.
Both denote the secondary title accompanying a main title; no literal title statement is produced.
